Calculating gradients of complex systems, such as those that cast shadows, is a computationally expensive and technically challenging task due to the need for a detailed analysis of how these gradients affect the overall system. This study presents a novel approach to determining accurate gradients of a shadow rendering process, which is based on a mathematical framework that calculates the distance between light sources and occluding objects along a set of rays. Experimental results demonstrate the high efficiency of this approach, which allows for practical use in advanced applications, such as recovering environmental factors from sensor data and performing related tasks.

Recent studies have demonstrated the effectiveness of probabilistic OD demand models in predicting traffic patterns. However, clear methods for estimating these models remain scarce. We develop a probabilistic OD demand model based on the Logit model and utilize traffic flow measurements from multiple origins and destinations to estimate OD demand distributions daily over an extended period. We demonstrate that this estimation process converges to a value related to the model's parameters as the time frame increases, allowing for reliable estimation of the model's parameters when sufficient data is available. We validate our model by applying it to real traffic data, showing successful predictions of OD demands and daily traffic patterns, as well as providing a framework to assess the reliability of estimations and predict future model evolution based on OD demands.

In an array of oscillators with uniform connections and no uniformity of frequencies, we observe that the system exhibits multiple synchronized states, where the oscillators' behavior is locked in specific patterns. To analyze this, we've developed a method to reduce the number of variables in the model by focusing on the most important factor influencing frequency variations. This reduction allows us to create simpler, two-variable models for specific types of oscillations. We then generalize our findings to complex systems with multiple degrees of freedom, using a new order parameter to measure synchronized states. This parameter reveals the presence of complex, higher-dimensional oscillations and provides insights into the relationship between the frequency dispersion and the amplitude of these intra-cluster oscillations.

The well-established algorithms by Aldous and Broder and Wilson generate uniform spanning trees (USTs) for a given graph in polynomial time. Although they serve this purpose, their unification and comparative performance remain poorly understood despite their simplicity. In a surprising development, it has been shown that a particular algorithm can simultaneously produce a uniform self-loop-free random walk and a UST in the same running time as the two algorithms individually. This dual algorithm operates in one step under specific conditions. A broader class of algorithms can achieve this equivalence, and such an algorithm can be devised to first run a modified version of the algorithm for a specific distribution of walk lengths. Next, it generates a UST in the same running time as producing the modified walk, all while maintaining the joint distribution of these two variables.

This work presents a comprehensive music dataset named MusicTM-Dataset, featuring colorfully labeled sheet music, corresponding sheet music annotations, and matching musical audio for every piece of music. Comprising sheet music and audio for 1,004 musical pieces and annotations of 7,229 bars in 699 labeled sheet music, our dataset fills a crucial gap by enabling diverse musical applications. An analysis of our dataset is accompanied yet, defining potential tasks and proposing methodologies for their accomplishment. A pioneering task called Joint Music Representation is also introduced, aiming to develop an effective sheet music representation that optimizes outcomes for both musical sheet and audio prediction. Notably, a baseline method utilizing a sheet music representation via vector graphics is provided, demonstrating its potential to significantly boost multi-objective learning performance.

One major obstacle when utilizing Linked Data lies in developing intuitive and user-friendly interfaces accessible to individuals who aren't technologically inclined. To address this, Ontodia enables diagrammatic data visualization, illustrated in this study with the Wikidata dataset. We've introduced enhancements to a natural language interface that facilitates the exploration and querying of Linked Data entities. By utilizing distributional semantic models to identify and rank entity properties associated with user input in Ontodia, the method demonstrates improved results in enhancing user experience during visual data exploration.

The stability of dark optical solitons in one-dimensional and two-dimensional systems with fixed or changing refractive indices is investigated through analytical and numerical methods, considering various types of soliton profiles and optical lattice configurations.

This study examines the concept of providing direct assistance in various tasks within an interactive environment. We present 'Lotse', a framework designed to offer assistance in different tasks within an interactive setting. Lotse provides a unified concept that encompasses multiple forms of assistance, including tailored recommendations and adaptive interface modifications. The framework's practical application is demonstrated through our system implementation, which offers assistance in different levels of expertise and enables the provision of assistance for novel combinations of tasks, techniques, and tools. We showcase the effectiveness of the Lotse framework using it to provide assistance with different tasks within the domains genomics and remote sensing.

We suggest an advanced method for optimizing the shape of stellarator coils to work with various coil arrangements and obtain optimal plasma results across multiple scenarios. This is achieved by incorporating coil shape parameters into a unified coil selection framework and using a consistent method to shape plasmas in all cases. A weighted approach in the objective function further ensures that coil currents remain low while still meeting goals for all desired plasma outcomes. Using simulated plasma data, we tested our method and found it successfully produces optimized coils and desirable plasma outcomes for each scenario, often with negligible trade-offs.

Our research presents a novel approach using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to visualize temperature variations within a fluidized bed. To make MRI feasible in hot environments, we have introduced a method involving the use of paramagnetic particles within the mixture. These particles enable the application of the CPMG pulse sequence to measure the transverse relaxation time of water in pore spaces. By analyzing these measurements, we can reconstruct the temperature profile inside the bed. The proposed technique has demonstrated the ability to resolve temperature differences of 10 K with a spatial resolution of around 1 mm. Our findings reveal the dynamic and heterogeneous nature of fluidized beds, with the system's temperature fluctuating more significantly than its overall temperature suggests.

Within a cell, proteins and nucleic acids form membraneless droplets, known as biomolecular condensates, through liquid-like phase transitions. These droplets play a crucial role in organizing cellular space and biochemistry. Although previous research has primarily focused on individual condensates, in reality, multiple droplets can form simultaneously, sharing components. A new study develops a theoretical framework to investigate the interactions between different phases, revealing the conditions under which components can be shared and how interactions between different molecules influence phase behavior. The model predicts that interactions between different components can induce transitions between different states, and further research using the Lean Protein Explorer database has shown that many proteins may participate in multi-component condensates, suggesting a previously unrecognized aspect of this phenomenon.

Using the Helioseismic and Magnetic Imager on the Solar Dynamics Observatory, we examined how a major leading sunspot rotated within a prominent sunspot group near the solar central meridian during a significant solar flare on March 7, 2018. As predicted by theory, the sunspot's rotation direction reversed after it passed from the eastern to western hemisphere. Additionally, we discovered that the sunspot's rotation speed increased due to the presence of fast-moving plasma structures generated by other sunspots, which were triggered by two other flares. By analyzing the changes in the sunspot's rotation, we were able to estimate the mass and velocity of these plasma structures and found that their properties matched those determined from farul spectra obtained by the Hinode telescope.

This note presents a new category of map functions known as oriented colored broken submersions, which forms the most basic type of map functions that adhere to the w-b-principle. It is demonstrated that the Mummford Conjecture, which can be rephrased as the inductive application of a stable map function classification by this category of broken submersions, constitutes the primary instance of the application of the w-b-principle in 3-manifolds. Furthermore, the Mummford Conjecture for 3-manifolds with Minkowski dimension 2 has already been proven by the first author in collaboration with Deninger and Welschinger.

This research paper investigates the efficiency of various multilevel preconditioners when solving cardiac mechanics problems, which involve intricate three-dimensional geometries and highly contrasting material properties. We stress the significance of incorporating problem-specific features into multilevel schemes to achieve optimal performance. Our study compares three multilevel methods: Algebraic Multigrid (AMG), geometric multigrid (H-adapted Multigrid-HAMG), and a recently developed Neural Network multigrid (NNMG). The performance of these preconditioners is evaluated in conjunction with two time-integration schemes for cardiac mechanics: the Backward Euler method and the Mass-lagged New-Rosenbrock scheme. The results show that AMG and HAMG, when properly adapted to the problem, deliver superior performance over conventional methods, while NNMG is shown to be a promising technique.

The ever-growing influence of user-generated content is significantly altering the digital landscape, with a particular focus on content management systems that handle vast amounts of loosely structured, user-created metadata. Analyzing the dynamics of tag evolution and collaboration patterns among users can offer valuable insights that drive tag system design. This research examines Flickr's cultural and organizational development through the lens of user behavior, exploring both the macro trends of photo tagging and micro trends of collaborative interest sharing. Key findings reveal that both the total number of tags and their distinct count exhibit exponential growth over time, with temporal tags clustering and displaying self-similarity characteristics. Additionally, clusters of tags show dynamic temporal behaviors, while photo sets demonstrate collaboration among users, with a preference for tags that persist over time and display a bias toward shorter lengths and higher frequencies.

Recently, there has been significant interest in acoustic metamaterials, particularly in research involving high-frequency Lithography. This research presents the design, simulation, and experimental investigation of microacoustic metagratings fabricated at 35 GHz using two-photon polymerization. The metagratings, fabricated using a high-precision method, consist of unit cells composed of two circular holes in a thin polymer layer attached to an aluminum substrate. The study demonstrates that these structures can effectively manipulate and concentrate surface acoustic waves, both in transmission and reflection modes. Notably, the research marks a significant milestone in acoustic metamaterial research by achieving the highest frequency operation, thus paving the way for their application in acoustic devices and integrated circuits.

This paper primarily focuses on the long-term behavior of strong solutions to the two-dimensional compressible FENE dumbbell model. Utilizing the Fourier splitting technique, we demonstrate that the $L^2$ decay rate is given by $\langle t \rangle^{-1}$ and that the rate is optimal. Additionally, under additional constraints, under the condition of being away from the essential spectrum, we demonstrate that the solution decays exponentially.

Integrating Integrated Access and Backhaul (IAB) in 5G networks via wireless backhaul can simplify and lower costs of deploying Integrated Access and Backhaul networks, making them suitable for mobile applications. However, the absence of a standard for mobile IAB has impeded its implementation in 5G networks, and thus, understanding the capabilities and limitations of mobile IAB is essential. A comprehensive study delves into the IAB architecture, base station connections, handover handling, and mobile IAB's potential applications and feasible scenarios. Additionally, it outlines the possible uses of IAB and suggests additional features and functions that could be integrated to further enhance its effectiveness.

In this study, we conduct an extensive examination of five different methods for hyperparameter optimization of Evolutionary Algorithms through global sensitivity analysis. The techniques under review include one screening method and four other methods for sensitivity measurement. The results highlight significant differences in the ranking of and importance to EA efficiency among the various methods, with the ranking of parameters also showing variation across different sensitivity analysis methods. Based on our findings, it's recommended that multiple sensitivity analysis methods be used to hyperparameter optimize evolutionary algorithms.

The paper addresses misconceptions surrounding Jefimenko's equations, which are mistakenly considered to contradict both Einstein's and Maxwell's equations. It first clarifies these errors, before exploring the implications of these equations for quantum theory, particularly focusing on whether a similar framework could be applied to the Schrödinger equation. The investigation leads to a non-standard equation, incorporating both time- and space-derivative intrinsics, and both theoretical and practical conundrums arising from this equation are discussed. The paper eventually investigates the possibility of a more complex, second-order time-derivative intrinsic replacing the first time-derivative in the standard Schrödinger equation.

Despite notable advancements in reinforcement learning, multiple obstacles persist,
including enhanced robustness and continuous learning capabilities. To address this,
we introduce L2Explorer, a new platform for creating complex environments that
incorporate randomised settings and novel, unforeseen tasks. This platform also
provides a range of evaluation tasks, emphasizing continuous learning and
parameter adaptation. It is particularly useful for developing more resilient
and adaptive reinforcement learning algorithms. An open-source implementation of
this platform is available on our GitHub repository at
https://github.com/CompEms/L2Explorer.

Liger, a next-generation infrared device at the W. M. Keck Observatory, features advanced imaging capabilities and will generate significant data. To handle this, a data reduction system is needed. We developed an open-source data reduction system based on PyRAF and IRAD, with a user-friendly interface called the web-based Reduction System Interface (web-RSI). This system is being tested on the Keck Observatory.

This study uncovers a broad class of non-trivial and smooth traveling wave solutions for the 2D Euler equation, occurring in a specific regime of high viscosity. The Coriolis force is present in this regime, whereas it is absent in the regime of low viscosity. The traveling waves discovered here cannot be equivalent to the Couette flow.

We experimentally control the linear polarization of exciton-polariton condensates using optical traps with elliptical geometries that favor specific polarization modes. Due to anisotropic splitting in the cavity, ground state degeneracy is lifted, yielding fine structure modes along the trap's axis and orthogonal to it, with different polarizations. These modes become competitive in different polarization directions, yielding a complete set of linear polarizations through experimental adjustment of the elliptical trap parameters. This mechanism for controlling polarizations can be scaled to two dimensions, enabling complex polarization patterns and all-optical processing of polarization information. Furthermore, by adding a second layer with parallel geometry, inter-cavity coupling modifies degeneracy and fine structure modes, yielding hybrid polarized condensates resulting from this two-dimensional engineering approach.

This study's primary objective is to demonstrate the existence and uniqueness of strong solutions for a class of stochastic partial differential equations influenced by noise and incorporating the derivative of a related function. The function in question is a specific measure of the average distance between related functions at nearby points. The authors' findings align with earlier research on similar equations discussed in related literature.

The emergence of the novel coronavirus in early 2020 triggered a global pandemic, exposing significant disparities in healthcare systems and social infrastructure among different countries. Effective mitigation of COVID-19 spread requires the timely implementation of non-pharmaceutical interventions, necessitating accurate diagnosis, surveillance, and data collection to forecast the outbreak's trajectory. Lack of real-time, reliable data hampers decision-making processes, as exemplified by South Africa's initial inaction due to unpreparedness. This study presents an analysis of data sources and collection methods utilized to combat COVID-19 in South Africa, emphasizing the critical need for a robust data management system to inform public health policies and save lives.

Freiman's 3k-4 theorem posits that if subsets A and B, of size k and comprised of integers, share a sumset A + B, whose cardinality is at most k + sqrt(2) times k, then A and B must be arithmetic progressions with the same difference. However, if we restrict the elements of A and B to be nonnegative, this conclusion can be drawn provided the constant is only slightly above k.

Recent advancements in deep learning have led to the widespread adoption of
convolutional neural networks in medical image analysis. Ocular diseases such as
diabetic retinopathy and glaucoma pose significant risks and early detection is
crucial to prevent irreversible vision loss. The primary methods for identifying
glaucoma involve assessing the neuro-retinal rim and the cup-to-disc ratio from
optical coherence tomography and fundus images, respectively. Diabetic
retinopathy can be detected by examining retinal abnormalities and
micro-aneurysms in fundus images. Despite the effectiveness of deep learning in
this field, most existing approaches focus on visual performance, often
neglecting performance explainability. In our study, we aim to enhance the
interpretation of our model's decisions through the use of attention heatmaps.
To achieve this, we employed two attention models: Grad-CAM and Attention Rollout.
The latter enables us to pinpoint and interpret the model's focus on anatomical
features and pathological signs in the images. The significance of our study
lies in its potential to highlight areas warranting clinical attention and
facilitate trustworthy decision-making in ophthalmic image analysis.

X-ray images contain subtle features that can aid clinical decision-making for COVID-19 patients, specifically whether they require admission to an ICU. Although the precise characteristics are not yet fully understood, their identification has the potential to improve treatment outcomes. This research aims to identify any distinguishable X-ray features that can accurately predict a patient's need for ICU care. A novel approach is proposed, where machine learning models are used to identify relevant image areas, and radiologists provide input on these areas to confirm their clinical significance. Characteristic X-ray features are then extracted and analyzed in association with patient data from an existing public dataset. A combination of image classifiers and radiologist input achieves accurate prediction of ICU requirements, with the interim results suggesting that lung involvement extent and location are key indicators. Further exploration is necessary to fully understand these features.

This study examines the transmission eigenvalues and functions of the Dirichlet Laplacian within the directional directions on spherically layered structures. Analyzing the directionally directed transmission spectrum, it is discovered that it's always discrete and positioned to the right of a unique, piecewise-defined and monotonically increasing sequence of eigenvalues. These sequence eigenvalues stem from the Neumann–Robin Laplacian on the same spherical layers. Moreover, it is proven that transmission functions exhibit complete boundary confinement at either the inner or outer boundary of the sphere at specific energies, identified as transmission eigenvalues. Additionally, it is demonstrated that only the ground states of the Dirichlet and Neumann–Robin Laplacians can yield transmission eigenvalues.

Current methods for discovering intent in conversation are limited to analyzing
predefined, fixed forms of input. However, users often express new ideas in
unconventional and unique ways, which challenges the applicability of existing
methods. To address this, we introduce a novel unsupervised approach that can
identify new, previously unseen categories of input based on similarities. By
leveraging pre-training on a large dataset and employing contrastive learning to
enhance the separation of input characteristics, we achieve superior results on
two publicly available conversation intent discovery benchmarks.

The classical universal bundle functor W mapping from the category of simplicial groups in C to the category of simplicial sets in C lifts to a monadic structure on the category of simplicial groups in C, and this extension holds for simplicial algebras defined by any Lawvere theory that includes group theory.
In our analysis, we demonstrate that a finite group of order $r$ possesses no more than $$7.3722\cdot r^{\frac{\log_2r}{4}+1.5315}$$ subgroups.

This study re-examines the Adler-Bobenko-Suris H2 equation. The equation has a direct linear relationship with the Cauchy matrix, allowing for various equivalent forms to be derived. By applying the Bäcklund transformation, distinct forms are obtained, which involve third-order differences. A newly devised lattice Sine-Gordon equation yields a Bäcklund transformation connecting the H2 equation with the Lattice KdP equation. Additionally, the discrete Lax pair for the Lattice KdP equation can be derived from that of the lattice Sine-Gordon equation, which leads to a simple Lax pair for the Adler H2 equation.

The Visual Relationship Detection task in NLP and CV involves identifying objects or regions in an image and the relationships between them. Current image relationship detection approaches face a significant challenge with false positives, in which unrelated objects are incorrectly associated. For example, a chair and a bed are sometimes wrongly linked by the phrase's chair on the bed. In this paper, we introduce the SVR dataset to address this issue. It consists of 5,200 scenes with 10,078 instances, covering a wider range of relationships between disjoint objects. To tackle the problem of false positives in VRD, we propose a new model, Transformer VLD, based on the Transformer encoder. It utilizes multi-head cross-attention to capture long-range dependencies and employs a novel loss function to calculate the compatibility between image features and language labels. Experimental results show that our model achieves state-of-the-art performance on the MS-COCO dataset and comparable or better performance than leading baselines on the SVR dataset.

A new measure, referred to as quantum correlation cost, has been developed for measuring quantum correlations associated with weak measurement interactions. This measure evaluates the minimal required quantum resource, analogous to quantum discord, and retains its quantum nature. It successfully identifies classically correlated states according to its value of zero, and demonstrates sensitivity to pointer shift. Furthermore, it accurately reflects the magnitude of the interaction Hamiltonian and period in specific scenarios, such as when using Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen pairs and performing weak Bell state measurements that demonstrate correlations equal to the product of final photon detection probabilities.

Artificial intelligence is revolutionizing the way companies interact with their customers, prompting many organizations to adopt AI-driven technologies. As a result, artificially-generated social data is proliferating online, raising significant ethical concerns. Although prior studies have focused on creating fake social media content and detecting its authenticity, the generation and identification of social relationship graphs remain unexplored. To address this gap, the researchers developed two novel models for generating social relationship graphs and a fourth model to detect them. The social relationship graph generation models leverage conditional generative adversarial networks to simulate realistic social interactions, while the detection model employs a generative discriminative framework. To test the efficacy of these models, the researchers assembled a dataset consisting of real and artificially-generated social relationship graphs from publicly available sources.

Capturing long-range connections in visual tasks is crucial to achieving top-notch performance, especially in scenarios like image, video, and sentence understanding. Current approaches mainly rely on self-attention networks, despite their success, they struggle with initial setup costs, fixed graph designs, and inefficient computation when processing long sequences. A new graph learning method, EdNet, has been proposed to overcome these limitations by dynamically generating graphs, allowing the model to learn and focus on long-range relationships effectively. By decoupling graph generation from the main network and assigning different nodes with distinct graph templates, EdNet can create diverse graphs and learn messages independently, all while maintaining efficient computation and back-propagation. When tested on various understanding scenarios, EdNet outperforms or matches state-of-the-art models, especially when paired with efficient edge pruning for longer sequences.

Optimizing hardware efficiency in digital circuits, specifically targeting the Multiple Constant Multiplication problem, is a key objective in computer architecture.  This optimization involves finding the best way to multiply several constants while minimizing the required hardware resources.  Existing solutions to the MCMP problem rely on two primary approaches: breaking down constants into simpler fractions using prime-based factorization, or employing binary representation, each with its own strengths.  To further improve upon these methods, we've developed a new digital circuit design that leverages a unique multiplier structure featuring multiple output bits from each stage.  This novel design allows us to integrate existing MCMP solutions more effectively, resulting in a substantial 10% average reduction in the hardware resources needed when comparing our new design to the state-of-the-art.

The intersection of quantum computing and deep neural networks has birthed a new field, blending the computational power of quantum circuits with the learning capabilities of artificial intelligence. This emerging field, known as quantum machine learning, is driven by the potential for exponential speedups in certain tasks, particularly those involving kernel-based methods. However, significant hurdles remain in developing practical quantum algorithms for optimization and data preparation, limiting the immediate impact of quantum neural networks (QNNs). This article provides an in-depth review of QNNs, offering a comprehensive survey that covers the fundamentals, various architectures, optimization techniques, and real-world applications, including a detailed analysis of the corresponding classical counterparts. It also explores the underlying theoretical challenges and future prospects, aiming to clarify complex concepts for researchers entering the field.

The radio frequency (RF) accelerator technology continues to be fundamental in 
high-energy physics (HEP) experiments, with a variety of strategies under 
consideration that will significantly influence future facilities. This 
covers not just the conventional tasks of cavity design and buffer storage 
installations, but also advanced techniques such as particle acceleration in 
tabletop plasmas and the development of compact, high-power superconducting 
accelerators. In this report, the current status of RF accelerator technology 
is detailed, along with identifying key challenges and opportunities where 
innovations could have transformative implications.

In the near future, physicists anticipate that the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) will discover new physics. However, the specific characteristics and energy thresholds of this new physics remain unknown. It's probable that insights gleaned from LHC data will require supplementary information obtained from a lepton collider to conduct a thorough investigation. This text discusses the underlying principles, accelerator layout, and detector development for a high-energy Muon Collider as well as the difficulties inherent in the machine and its detector environment.

We have determined the dispersion relations for relativistic fluid modes in various configurations - scalar, vector, and tensor - and found the differences between their behavior in divergence-based and relaxation-time-approximation models. The latter accurately captures direction-dependent properties, particularly for vector and tensor modes. However, the models agree on certain combinations of direction and frequency that characterize tensor modes, suggesting that the distinction between them is primarily due to higher-order shape corrections rather than damping rates. This agreement provides some support for using divergence-based theories to study the effect of fluid interactions on horizon dynamics in black hole systems, despite potential discrepancies in both mechanisms and relaxation times.

Our research examines whether the cosmic background of Hawking radiation from primordial black holes can be responsible for the observed increase in the strength of the effect described by the law $S_{\text{sky}} = -0.28^\prime \cdot B_V + 1.75$ (Kaspi et al.2015). By modeling the temperature of the universe and calculating the emission and absorption rates of the emitted photons, we demonstrate that the radiation does not significantly contribute to the observed data. Further calculations projecting the future evolution of the universe's temperature reveal that, in the distant future, the effect could potentially become a dominant factor in determining the sky temperature.

Introducing the Virtual Secure Platform (VSP), a pioneering solution that brings together cryptographic cryptography and advanced circuit design to create a secure platform for computation. Building on an existing platform, VSP incorporates the SecretFlow framework, integrating it as a multi-cycle processor with a five-stage pipeline to offer isolated and ciphertext-based computation capabilities. As the first processor implementation of SecretFlow's TFHE scheme, VSP features architecture, digital circuit design, and instruction set design tailored for TFHE. This work details the design process, performance analysis, innovations, and security enhancements of VSP, marking a significant step forward in securing computation platforms.

Research into the complexity of solving value counting problems for general-valued constraint satisfaction problems (CSPs) is an active area of study. We address a key approximation result by deriving a polynomial time approximation scheme (PTAS) for a specific subset of CSPs, characterized by the absence of trivial constraints and limited connectivity in the constraint interaction graph. Notably, our result extends the existing range of tractable CSP subclasses, particularly those with binary constraints. Our approach builds on the framework of correlation clustering but introduces an novel round-based constraint evaluation strategy.

This study presents unsupervised and few-shot dependency parsing models that leverage pre-trained language models, such as BERT and XLNet. Given a pretrained language model and optionally some syntactically-labeled data, these models generate a dependency parse of an input sentence by producing an unsupervised dependency parser or a few-shot dependency parser. The performance of the proposed approach is substantially better than that of a strong alternative, relying solely on pre-trained language models without any supplementary syntactic data for training. Specifically, on few-shot datasets, our results show that this method outperforms a strong baseline by a notable 3.11-F scores in dependency scores and 2.84-F scores in head dependency labels, among other languages. Crucially, our models utilize minimal amounts of annotated data, amounting to less than 0.5% of the total dataset size.

High-definition hyperspectral images serve as an excellent source of semantic details. Nevertheless, their widespread adoption in real-world applications is hindered by the exorbitant costs associated with acquiring such data sets. This paper presents a novel approach to leverage the abundant high-resolution RGB images and a limited set of hyperspectral images for achieving semantic segmentation on a cityscape platform. Our technique harnesses the full spectral information from the hyperspectral images to train a neural network, which then utilizes these features to generate a semantic segmentation framework that effectively works on both RGB and hyperspectral images. The proposed method proves to be more efficient than existing weakly-supervised techniques in terms of accuracy, while also enabling a ratio of labeled hyperspectral images to total images that amounts to under 5%. Additionally, our approach yields a remarkable result on the cityscape dataset, achieving a mIoU score of 38.1, which is second only to the state-of-the-art fully-supervised method that yields a mIoU score of 40.2.

This study reveals that a massive star, having exhausted its core nuclear reactions, has unexpectedly maintained rapid rotation, a phenomenon at odds with standard stellar evolution models. These models suggest a rapidly dying star should lose its rotation quickly, but instead, a core-collapse supernova is thought to be the cause of its present-day spin. A previous study proposed an alternative explanation, suggesting the star's rapid rotation could be the result of a planet or small star being engulfed. While this hypothesis fits the observed data, a crucial question remains: how did the object acquire the enormous amount of angular momentum required to influence the star's rotation? To address this, we have developed a simple theoretical model describing how the angular momentum is transferred from the engulfed object to the star's surface. The model indicates that as the object migrates inward, it causes the surrounding stellar envelope to expand and rotate more quickly, consistent with the observed data. Moreover, the interaction between the object and the stellar material it passes through becomes increasingly unstable as the object moves closer to the star, potentially leading to the transfer of the object's entire angular momentum to the star's surface. Our study suggests that the engulfment of the object may provide a plausible explanation for the star's unusual rotation, but the answer to how the object acquired its angular momentum in the first place remains an open question.

In the analysis of algorithms, a common model is the word-RAM model, but understanding the true computational power of its basic operations has proven challenging. We made a key advancement in this area by investigating which fundamental operations can be executed in the RAM model, incorporating specific functions such as bitwise operations and div. We identified that a specific set of functions includes all operations executable in constant time, specifically examining functions like finding the least significant one, extracting, shifting, and reversing the positions of binary digits in another function, along with the ability to perform division and modulo operations.

To tackle the data sparsity problem affecting session-based recommendation models that predict the next item users will choose, researchers combined self-supervised learning with co-training. They proposed an enhanced framework by leveraging a session-based graph to create informative, not artificially sparse, data for these models. This new approach exploits internal and external session connections to produce contrastive learning, thereby preserving genuine data for superior session-based recommendation performance. Evaluations on three real-world datasets demonstrated the success of this method in achieving state-of-the-art session-based recommendation results.

This research presents a novel method for generating LCD codes using group rings and a standard transformation that maps group ring components to a subring of $n \times n$ matrices, resulting in LCD codes that are also group codes with a controllable minimum distance. The concept of reversibility in group codes is introduced, leading to the definition of reversible LCD codes and an group code transformation that preserves these properties. It is shown that the mapping from group ring elements to matrices yields LCD codes, with controllable minimum distance achieved when this distance in the group code equals the minimum distance of the group ring code. Furthermore, a dual mapping is considered, producing reversible LCD codes under specific conditions. Various examples and accompanying parity-check matrices are provided to illustrate the findings.

We examine differential forms on an algebraic compactification of the complete graph complex, defined by Cheah-Eriksson-Henn. These forms are generated by Henn's loop expansion differential forms and display notable properties. The forms are shown to be invariant under graph isomorphisms and, despite having singularities, exhibit exceptional behavior when restricted to each individual Feynman graph's completion. The forms are verified to be closed on the entire graph complex and on specific sub-complexes, namely the 2-propagator graphs, 2-treeless graphs, and forest graphs. The forms are demonstrated to satisfy the Kreimer relation when restricted to forest graphs. The forms on 2-propagator graphs and 2-treeless graphs satisfy the Kreimer and Chen-Ruan relations, and on forest graphs, they exhibit the Chen-Ruan and Chen-Steenrod relations, and a variant of the pull-back formula of Chevalley and Eisenberg-Tobisch. The forms are shown to relate to Henn's multiple zeta values.

A key challenge in developing robust object recognition models for diverse settings
is separating object category information from other factors like background and
object position.  Recurrent neural networks (RNNs) are an effective tool for learning
the dynamics of visual processing, yet it's unclear how they behave in complex
environments.  This study investigates how an object-centered version of a classic
visual model, the HMAX object recognizer, behaves when integrated into a simple
recurrent structure.  We discover that this integration leads to models that
outperform previous state-of-the-art baselines in difficult object recognition tasks.
Moreover, these state-of-the-art models consistently separate object category
information from other influencing factors during learned computations, mirroring
how humans and other animals process object-related information in the brain.  Our
findings suggest that recurrent structures can be employed in complex environments
to achieve robust, category-centered object recognition in line with biological
observations.

We investigate the impact of correlations on one-dimensional non-Hermitian models exhibiting point-based topological characteristics. Our findings demonstrate that one- and two-body correlations can induce a topological phase transition in an established model. Unlike symmetric many-body states, which are capable of being mapped to non-interacting systems with particular characteristics, generic many-body states exhibit unique topological properties that cannot be directly associated with their single-particle components. To address this complexity, we introduce a many-body wave function method based on a product of wave function amplitudes, which we apply to the Hofstadter model with non-Hermitian properties. Our study reveals that in the ground state of this model, the wave function amplitude gradually decreases, which is in contrast to its Hermitian counterpart.

Recently, Golay complementary matrices of the K-times phased version were introduced, however this comes at the cost of a higher polynomial degree. Our research develops novel formulas to generate $F_2$ and $F_3$ polyphase GCAs of length three and higher, with the goal of creating higher order polynomial expressions. Our research also showcases how these new constructions can be applied to create polyphase complementary configurations in practical scenarios such as phased Golay radar and sonar arrays.

The production and decay characteristics of the Higgs boson are analyzed in the
four-lepton final state, utilizing proton-proton collision data with 125 GeV
center-of-mass energy collected at the Large Hadron Collider. The analysis, based
on 139 inverse femtobarns of collected data, distinguishes between Higgs boson and
background events in the $Z$-boson mass and off-mass regions. The findings are
interpreted through both standard and extended model parameters, yielding the
following results: the Higgs boson production coupling to vector bosons is
consistent with theoretical predictions, with a 1.34 times off-scale factor,
while the Higgs boson decay width is estimated at 3.90 MeV, with a 31 MeV uncertainty.
Additionally, the production and non-two-body decay coupling strengths are
estimated at -0.013 and -0.015, with respective uncertainties of 0.010 and 0.012.

Incorporating dimensionality reduction techniques, researchers address the complexities of analyzing numerous spectral bands within bi-temporal hyperspectral images. This study proposes a cutting-edge approach using a novel deep convolutional autoencoder that fuses features across hierarchical levels and receptive fields. By utilizing an unsupervised change detection technique, it overcomes the limitations of other label-dependent methods. By integrating various techniques to extract changes from the images, it significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art methods in unsupervised change detection across numerous datasets.

Consider the set $\mathcal{Q}$, defined as all non-negative integers that can be expressed as a square. Theorem 1 states that for any integer $k$ or larger, there exists a subset $\mathcal{R}$, also of cardinality $k$, with the property that the sum of any $\mathcal{Q}$ element and any $\mathcal{R}$ element is not a square. The size of $\mathcal{R}$ is bounded above by $2^{\frac{4+o(1)}{3}k}$. This is the best result achievable as the growth rate of $\mathcal{R}$ is optimal by virtue of a previous finding by Baur and Beiglböck.

Quantum tunneling of ions between valley states in silicon creates visible patterns 
of spin exchange, providing a way to read out valley degrees of freedom. This 
exchange interaction varies significantly between different valley states, producing 
an oscillating pattern as ions move between sites. The pattern's amplitude and 
periodicity can be controlled by changing the lattice structure, encoding valley 
coherences in the matter wave phase and dictacting their potential applications in valleytronics.

Several domains heavily rely on optimization techniques to tackle complex problems.
Islands of local optima, convex-relaxation methods, and iterative approaches are among the methods employed to address optimization problems.
However, real-world applications often require incorporating uncertainties, extending solutions to non-convex formulations, and minimizing latency, making it difficult to achieve optimal results.
To address these challenges, we introduce a new framework called LibOPT, a versatile and open-source tool for efficiently prototyping advanced optimization techniques.
LibOPT supports an open architecture, easy integration of new methods, and relevant supporting tools, such as simulated annealing and stochastic gradient methods.
It also features time-critical variants of methods, including parallel, vectorized, and hierarchical versions, to minimize processing time.
We apply LibOPT to solve an IoT data collection problem, outperforming industry 4.0 solutions and achieving superior results compared to methods like simulated annealing and gradient descent.

Given an algebraic variety X that has a transitive action from the group Aut(X), the highest degree of transitivity of this action is called the transitivity degree. This degree is denoted by the maximum value of m for which Aut(X) acts transitively m times on X. In cases where Aut(X) is m-transitive for any positive value of m, we define the transitivity degree to be infinite. This study involves determining the transitivity degree for specific varieties, such as quasi-affine toric varieties, and homogeneous spaces, while exploring related open problems and conjectures.

In non-commutative space-time deformations, the definition of identical particles breaks down. These models are based on an algebra of space-time symmetries that, when deformed, cannot describe the same particle for all momenta. We show that the non-commutative evolution equations for particle states have a solution, but the resulting currents cannot form an invariant, non-commutative version of the conservation law. This breaks the basis for defining isolated, identical particles at different momenta. The problem arises from the inability to define free particle states for all momenta, and thus their superpositions. This limits the usefulness of non-commutative space-time models in particle physics, and we suggest possible resolutions.

We demonstrate the capability of combining two-photon absorption with an optical pumping transient voltage/current measurement technique to induce localized charge in high-quality single-phase diamond. By fine-tuning the synthesis and heat treatment process, we were able to pinpoint and quantify native diamondystalline charge carriers as well as introduce external acceptor dopants within the vanadium range, achieving controlled p-type conductivity. This results in a significant increase in mobility for hole conduction, up to 10 cm^2/Vs. The technique's precision allows us to create intricate patterns of transient voltage/current measurements and track the complex interaction and transport properties of these charge carriers in three dimensions in real-time.

This research focuses on developing a set of specialized classifiers for identifying and categorizing misogynistic content in texts from social media platforms. The study builds on a comprehensive dataset of Arabic social media text, meticulously labeled by domain experts with fine-grained tags. These labels enable the creation of four distinct tasks: detecting hate speech targeting women, pinpointing mentions of specific genders, distinguishing between different levels of hostility, and pinpointing references to particular groups. By employing three advanced deep learning models, the research demonstrates the potential for models to excel in these intricate classification and extraction tasks, ultimately outperforming traditional machine learning algorithms and enabling the model to achieve state-of-the-art results in misogyny identification.

This study centres around the solvability of a distinct class of fractional backward stochastic differential equations that take into account past influences within their generators, under Lipschitz condition it's demonstrated that the existence and uniqueness of such equations are assured. Furthermore, a key comparison theorem has been formulated.

We examine if controllers obtained using model-based Reinforcement Learning, which employs an environment model to find the optimal policy, remain robust and adaptable when dealing with slight environmental variations. Building upon the concept from PILCO, a method for probabilistic policy search, our research demonstrates that constraining the uncertainty in the Gaussian Process model's dynamics has a beneficial effect on policy updates and results in more resilient controllers. In addition, our findings highlight the practical advantages of this approach in a simulation-based evaluation.

This research presents a unified method for designing and analyzing both coded caching and distributed computation schemes, utilizing a binary matroid $\mathcal{M}$ with $N$ elements and $F$ lines, where $N$ represents the number of files and $F$ denotes the number of distinct subsets, such as caches or server computations. The method covers prefetching, subpacketization, download, Compressed Distributed Computing (CDC), and download enhancement phases. A key aspect of our approach involves introducing a code $\mathcal{C}$ based on matroid lines, which serves as an essential tool for our design method. We provide an illustrative example using a projective plane of order $q$ and compare it with the coded caching scheme from [Ji et al. 2019]. Our unified method enables a clearer understanding of existing schemes and may lead to new insights.

We establish a formalization of the Scott model in univalent type theory, adopting a constructive and predicative framework. To capture the essence of non-terminating processes in PCF, we employ the lifting monad from topos theory, which has been adapted for univalent type theory by Escard\'o and Knapp. Our work confirms that using subtypes to model continuous functions aligns with the standard understanding in domain theory. Moreover, we prove the uniqueness up to equivalence of functions with arbitrary partiality types, thereby enabling a fully predicative approach. This adaptation also allows for the definition of predicates in univalent type theory, which are distinct from general subtypes and facilitate proofs of properties like continuity and monotonicity for functions with partiality.

Hanzer and Muić's work on degenerate Eisenstein series cancellations has been built upon, 
extending their method and outcome to a specific set of Eisenstein series, 
specifically those formed from the combinations of two Speh representations 
for $GL(n,\mathbb{Q}_p)$, where $n$ is an even number, 
by utilising the recursive cancellation method that is central to the Parshin's conjecture and the elements at infinity in Eisenstein series cancellations.

Designing effective collision avoidance systems for mobile robots remains a key challenge, particularly when accounting for the robot's shape and orientation, which can vary as it moves. Traditional methods using the Configuration-Aware Potential Function Field (C-PFF) consider the robot's shape and orientation, but they often fail to guarantee safe paths and smooth trajectories, particularly for mobile robots whose paths are constrained by kinematic constraints. To address this limitation, we propose a novel approach that combines C-PFF with Control Barrier Functions (CBF) quadratic programs (CBF-QPs). CBF-QPs use the C-PFF-derived CBF constraints to create a safe control input that considers the robot's shape and orientation. We demonstrate the proposed approach through simulations of a differential-driven mobile robot carrying a manipulator arm through a complex environment.

Natural language processing, a crucial field of study, strives to comprehend text via digital analysis, despite the inherent imperfections arising from diverse forms of written and spoken language. This work delves into employing various graph-based methodologies for resolving the challenge of text summarization via a selective extraction technique. Two key indicators – sentence overlap and edit distance – are employed for gauging sentence similarity.

Researchers have shown significant interest in the application of Bose-Einstein condensates for the development of quantum computing, particularly due to the presence of a Kerr nonlinearity in BECs. This property allows for the creation of single-qubit gates, and researchers have successfully implemented a key-Bernoulli unitary gate using this method. However, the control of entangling gates and entangled states remains limited, primarily due to the inability to implement a entangling gate based on Kerr nonlineality alone. This research presents a solution to these challenges by introducing a new nonlinear entangling gate, the key-Bernoulli entangling gate, which utilizes Kerr nonlineality in conjunction with an additional control parameter. This gate, along with its associated control parameter, enables the creation of entangled, superposition, and mixed states from an arbitrary initial quantum state. Furthermore, the study outlines the implementation of this entangling gate through the controlled manipulation of an optical probe and an RF signal applied to a BEC.

This paper aims to accomplish two distinct objectives. Firstly, it seeks to establish a unicity theorem for meromorphic mappings from a complete Kähler manifold to a complex projective space, under the constraint of limited intersection with an ample hypersurface family. Secondly, the paper aims to prove a unicity theorem for the case of non-degenerate meromorphic mappings from a complete Kähler manifold to a complex projective space, where the images of these mappings intersect with hyperplanes in a specified manner.

A signature is a useful tool for analyzing polynomial systems, and it can be utilized to determine the non-degenerate locus, which is the set of values for the parameters for which the system has a certain number of solutions in a particular space. To compute the nondegenerate locus, a new algorithm is developed that involves finding the elimination ideal of a polynomial system, which is then used to find the nondegenerate locus via a well-known computation method. The algorithm is implemented in the Computer Algebra System Singular and uses a different solving method based on certified non-degeneracy. The order of the elimination ideal and the time required for the new algorithm are determined and found to be consistent with the bounds for Gröbner basis computation.

Direct photons have been measured at $p_T<5$ GeV/$c$ for midrapidity and most central ranges of $dN/dy$ in Cu$+$Cu collisions at $\sqrt{s_{_{NN}}}=200$ GeV.  This study found that the measured direct photon spectrum matches nearly with the inclusive photon spectrum, but significantly exceeds the expectation from order-$\alpha_s$ calculations.  Radiative energy loss of hard partons due to the medium is found to be consistent with inclusive photon measurements and provides evidence for the strong interaction of high-energy partons with the quark-gluon plasma.  Cross-checking with more theoretical models revealed that initial and final state radiation contribute equally, and production of photons from soft partons interacting with hot QCD matter is suppressed at $dN_\gamma^{\rm direct}/dp_T<1$ GeV/$c$.  Radiation from $dN_\phi^{\rm direct}/dp_T < 0.5$ GeV/$c$ is found to be insensitive to the specifics of radiation processes.

The Turan tetrahedron issue was first addressed by N. Alon and J. Hsiang with an  $O(n^{6.25})$-size lower bound.
This paper presents a construction that achieves an $\Omega(n^{6.1925})$ lower bound by utilizing the $\ell_2$-norm.
This result is accomplished through an extension of the technique developed for the Turan cone problem by M.
Balogh, M. Nashef, and the second author.

One key aspect that influences visual quality in vector rendering is spatial anti-aliasing, 
which is particularly crucial for creating smooth line joins in maps. Although some vector 
graphics formats support spatial anti-aliasing for line joins, many still neglect it, 
resulting in suboptimal visual quality. This study analyzes the root causes of spatial 
aliasing in line joins and its visual effects, and proposes an innovative, high-performance 
method to resolve it, called EARL, with support already integrated into GeoJSON. EARL 
achieves superior visual quality and up to 1.8x performance improvement compared to existing 
techniques, and is open-source available on GitHub at https://github.com/Esri/earl, 
along with its corresponding JS and Swift libraries.

The multivariate interpolation operator is traditionally constructed using piecewise linear functions to approximate absolute first-order derivatives. In this study, we develop a novel, transcendental multiquadratic radial basis function, whose global absolute first-order derivatives converge uniformly to the absolute second-order derivatives as the shape parameter approaches zero. This property enables us to define an innovative, global, bounded, and shape-preserving multivariate interpolation scheme based on the first-order derivatives of this radial basis function, with the resulting global absolute first-order derivatives accurately approximating the absolute second-order derivatives. Consequently, this interpolation scheme is particularly suitable for solving partial differential equations, with the global absolute first-order derivatives converging at a rate of O(η^α) to the original function, where η and α respectively represent the mesh size and the smoothness of the original function.

Pulsar wind nebulae formed at the base of powerful stellar energies release jets that propagate upwards, creating expansive halos of high-energy particles. These particles eventually collide with surrounding interstellar radiation, emitting traceable gamma-rays. Observatories like Fermi-LAT, HESS, HESS-2, and CTA have detected signs of these gamma-ray pulsar halos, and future observations with larger telescopes and larger arrays are expected to confirm their presence. Research into pulsar halos will provide valuable insights into the complex physics occurring within the Galactic plane.

Classification of weather is a crucial task with far-reaching effects on various fields, including video surveillance, home automation, and computer vision. This research presents a novel multi-class weather dataset, novel data augmentation techniques, and an extensive evaluation of widely-used Convolutional Neural Networks. Our findings reveal that cutting-edge networks, such as ResNet-50, achieve exceptional results on our custom dataset, reaching 97.8% accuracy, and the proposed data augmentation method yields 96.9% accuracy. The source code for this work can be accessed at https://github.com/rodrigo-oliveira-oliveira/Weather-Detection.

Our analysis examines how climate change affects social norms, institutions,
and economic factors through three distinct but interconnected processes.
These processes are influenced by different mechanisms: one driven by
scientific information, another by international social pressure, and the
third by market forces. Our model demonstrates how these processes can
reinforce or counteract each other, affecting the outcome of climate change
policy and the transition to a low-carbon economy. Our three processes also
give rise to multiple equilibria, implying that multiple pathways can be taken
to achieve a target outcome, and that the target may not be reached
automatically through these processes. Our study highlights the potential
role of a target outcome as a social norm, and the influence of institutions
in promoting low-carbon technologies market-wide. Our evaluation reveals that
the target norm can be promoted through mechanisms including market forces,
scientific information, and international social pressure, with institutions
playing a crucial role in advancing this goal.

Soft grippers, thanks to their versatility and adaptability, are gaining attention for use in industrial settings and service robotics applications. However, accurately controlling their behavior remains challenging. A novel solution, the integration of data-driven control techniques, specifically the offline model prediction control technique, is proposed for multi-fingered soft grippers. A data-driven, nonlinear dynamic model, the Koopman model, is developed to simulate and control the control points of the Finite Element Model, which models the gripper's behavior. By leveraging the spectral theory of Koopman operators, the model learning process, although initially complex, is made more feasible. A model-based controller, the Infinite Horizon Model Predictive Control, is subsequently developed to ensure stable control and convergence to the equilibrium point. Simulation and experimental outcomes validate the efficacy of the Online-MPC-MK approach.

One of the fundamental problems in science and engineering involves finding the minimum of differentiable functions, a task commonly addressed through Gradient Descent (GD). However, GD may struggle when dealing with constrained parameters, such as those in Reinforcement Learning, which often require methods like Natural Gradient Descent (NGD). Our study presents a novel framework that generalizes NGD, offering the flexibility to incorporate various forms of descent directions and 'metrics'. This framework not only encompasses NGD as a special case but also allows for the integration of the Gradient Lifted on Correlation and the Riemannian Gradient Descent. Building upon this generalized framework, we derive theoretical convergence guarantees for different scenarios, including smooth and non-smooth functions, as well as constrained optimization problems. Our extensive experiments validate the effectiveness of the proposed solution, especially when implementing the Correlation Descent, outperforming both NGD and Gradient Lifted on Correlation in real-world constrained optimization tasks.

High-energy emissions from powerful AGN, including radio, X-ray, and gamma-ray, provide significant insights into the growth of black holes and jets. Research has established a significant correlation between high-energy emissions and the environment surrounding AGN, as well as the characteristics of jets and their power. Although many radio-selected samples at redshifts greater than 2.5 have been discovered, there is limited information available on AGN and jets in these discoveries. A newly identified radio source, designated J2102+6015, has been discovered at a redshift of 4.575 with extensive observations and accurate measurement of its energy and energy. This discovery was made through the utilization of the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array and the Hyper-CAM. Observations in radio, infrared, and X-ray wavelengths have been conducted to analyze the energy and environment of J2102+6015. This discovery is consistent with other high-z radio sources in terms of energy and energy, as well as in terms of the Hadronic model for AGN.

This study proposes an innovative approach for predicting survival outcomes in patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) by combining multiple complementary data sources. The method utilizes a neural network to analyze histopathological images and another that processes clinical data, integrating the results to improve the accuracy of prognosis. The proposed model outperforms existing methods in terms of predictive accuracy and reduces the time required for patient assessment by automatically extracting relevant information from digital histopathology slides and medical records.

A well-designed state representation is crucial in the learning process of Reinforcement Learning. Natural language can be utilized in numerous tasks to either represent the state or constitute it entirely. This overview focuses on the techniques employed by researchers to create natural language state representations, underscoring the need for more transparent and contextualized models, thorough justification of design choices and assessments of the relative effectiveness of varying methods.

A novel approach combining machine learning is introduced, enabling the accurate reconstruction of high-redshift cosmological density perturbations through observed quasar spectra analysis. By leveraging this method, an effective reconstruction algorithm can be developed, initially tested with synthetic data and then applied to actual data, revealing the associated reconstruction errors. Furthermore, this study investigates various factors influencing quasar sampling bias, facilitating further research into quasar sampling's impact on cosmological power spectrum estimation.

This paper examines certain types of non-weight modules connected to Lie algebras of the Weyl type. Firstly, we establish the characteristics of modules whose underlying spaces are algebras of differential operators, a concept linked to the work of Futorny and Ostanik. We then identify the underlying spaces of these modules as specific sheaves of algebras, characterized by Shapovalov and Shchekin. Lastly, we explore the module structure of the universal enveloping algebra of $\mathfrak h$, viewed as a commutative Lie algebra, in relation to the Weyl algebra, and establish a connection to the study of free modules over it.

Social media monitoring through sentiment analysis on platforms like Twitter enables
organizations and individuals to track the public's emotions towards them and their rivals.
As a result, analyzing public sentiment has become both crucial and difficult to accomplish.
In this project, we gathered and manually annotated seven distinct sentiment categories from
unprocessed Twitter data: extremely negative, very negative, neutral, very positive, and
extremely positive. An Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model was then developed to
efficiently classify these sentiments. The proposed model outperformed the current state-of-the-
art methods, showcasing its superiority in the classification task.

Recent advances in open-domain dialogue systems have significantly outperformed traditional systems, largely due to the incorporation of large-scale language models. While this type of dialogue system can facilitate natural and engaging conversations, some systems may cause discomfort in open-domain conversations with individuals who have specific communication preferences. For example, some people prefer systems that do not consistently agree with their opinions. To address this limitation, we propose a novel approach to enhance the inclusivity of natural dialogue systems by incorporating the principles of basic social psychology. To validate our method, we have developed a dataset containing dialogue exchanges between individuals and someone adhering to the principles of the Gricean Maxims. We then compare the effectiveness of our proposed method to that of standard dialogue systems in terms of human evaluations of engagement, and also investigate the systems' abilities to identify role-specific language patterns.

The binary black hole population has been verified as the primary source of background noise in recent detections by LIGO and Virgo. The fundamental cause of both the background noise and the signals from these binary black holes is the gravitational wave memory effect. The magnitude of the memory effect is roughly proportional to the overall change in strain, which can be around 10% for both the stochastic signal and the memory effect. Because of this proportionality, it's possible to have a significant memory effect even when the strain is as low as 10 times the threshold of detection. The time duration of the memory effect signal lasts about an order of magnitude longer than the main oscillatory part. The magnitude of the memory effect signal is roughly around 1% of the peak amplitude of the main oscillatory part. The characteristics of the memory effect signal follow the distribution of the final velocity of the binary black holes after merger, with low-velocity black holes producing a long-lasting, low-amplitude signal, and high-velocity black holes generating a stronger, short-lived signal. The characteristic duration of the memory effect signal during the inspiral and merger phases is about an order of magnitude longer than the peak duration of the main oscillatory part. The magnitude of the memory effect signal during the inspiral and merger is roughly around 10% of the peak amplitude of the main oscillatory part, with the signal following the shape of the main oscillatory part.
